messages:
amanda: Quick weekly rollup — small heads-up before EOD deploys. We're changing the default continuous-batching target from 128 -> 96 for text-generation routes to reduce tail-latency spikes seen on r5 nodes. No schema changes. Plan: rollout in 3 phases (us-east, europe, apac) starting 2026-03-29 18:00 UTC. Expect a 5-10% QPS drop on first pass; autoscale should compensate. If you own a route with <200ms p50 SLA, please opt into the "preserve-latency" flag in your service config or ping me.
kevin: @amanda can you paste the rollout playbook link? also will this affect embeddings endpoints?
amanda: embeddings unaffected — only generation pipelines. playbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/batching-rollout-3ph
release-bot: Deploy scheduled by amanda at 2026-03-29T18:00:00Z. Canary batch: us-east-1 on r5-gpu-4. Monitoring targets: latency, 5xx, request_queuing.
maria: Noted. I'll flag routes with strict SLAs in the inventory and DM owners.
jon: How do we opt into preserve-latency? quick snippet?
amanda: add env var in service-config: "PRESERVE_LATENCY=true" or set route-level config: batch.target=96 ; example:

```
route:
  name: /generate/chat
  batch:
    target: 96
flags:
  PRESERVE_LATENCY: "true"
```
kevin: thx. I'll run a quick local smoke on staging tomorrow morning.
amanda: Thanks — if anything looks off deploy team will pause after phase 1. Tag me with :loudspeaker: or DM. I'll post a short summary in #incidents if we see regressions.
